key_insight: Trotterized time evolution and QPE can preserve symmetry more reliably when the Hamiltonian is rewritten with Hermitian excitation operators, but non-Abelian symmetries may still require additional operator restructuring.
engineering_relevance: The result helps quantum algorithm designers choose symmetry-conserving operator pools and Trotter schemes that reduce simulation error in quantum chemistry and other many-body fermionic problems.
method: Rewrite the Hamiltonian as Hermitian excitation operators.
Map these operators to sums of commuting Pauli strings for arbitrary encodings.
Apply "operator kirigami"—orthogonal projection and unitary rotations—to handle non-commuting terms and improve symmetry handling.
evidence_signal: The authors tested operator pools on small molecules and basis sets, finding that symmetry-conserving pools produced larger errors that diminished for larger molecules and were removed with second-order Trotterization.
watch_item: Non-Abelian symmetries are not fully preserved by Trotterized Hermitian excitation operators, so implementation details and Trotter order still matter.
paper_title: Symmetry conservation with Trotterization and Quantum Phase Estimation
